title: Inference Engineering
license: Free to read online, all rights reserved (Baseten Labs, Inc.)
why: A survey of the full inference stack: GPUs, engines like vLLM and SGLang, quantization, speculative decoding, KV cache and production serving.
notes: Free to read on Baseten's site. Print copies are sold separately.

title: Dive into Deep Learning
authors: Aston Zhang, Zachary C. Lipton, Mu Li, Alexander J. Smola
license: Free online (text CC BY-SA 4.0, code MIT, per the d2l-en repo)
why: Every chapter pairs the math with runnable PyTorch, JAX or TensorFlow code, from basics through transformers.

title: Understanding Deep Learning
why: Clear modern treatment of deep learning, transformers, diffusion and RL with strong figures and no hand-waving.

title: Deep Learning: Foundations and Concepts
why: Bishop's modern rewrite covering transformers, diffusion and generative models with the same careful math.
notes: Free web reader. The PDF ebook is paid.

title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
why: The best short walk through backpropagation and why networks learn, built up from scratch in Python.
notes: From 2015, before transformers. Still the clearest intro to the core mechanics.

title: The Little Book of Deep Learning
why: A compact reference that fits on a phone screen and covers the whole modern toolbox in about 160 pages.

title: Deep Learning
authors: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville
license: Free online, all rights reserved (MIT Press)
why: The standard reference for the theory behind neural networks, optimization and regularization.
notes: From 2016, before transformers. Read it for fundamentals.

title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders (fastbook)
license: Free notebooks, copyright held by the authors
why: Top-down, code-first route to training real models quickly, then going back to the theory.

title: Alice's Adventures in a Differentiable Wonderland, Volume I
why: A friendly, code-oriented tour of differentiable programming that ends at convolutions, attention and transformers.

title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python
authors: Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jonathan Taylor
why: The gentlest rigorous start to regression, classification, trees and resampling, with Python labs.

title: Speech and Language Processing (3rd ed. draft)
license: Free draft chapters and single PDF, copyright the authors
why: The standard NLP textbook, updated through LLMs, attention, pretraining and post-training.

title: Foundations of Large Language Models
why: A textbook-length account of pre-training, generative models, prompting, alignment and inference.

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (2nd ed.)
authors: Richard S. Sutton, Andrew G. Barto
license: Free PDF from the authors (MIT Press)
why: The foundational text on agents that learn from reward, which underlies RLHF and modern agent training.

title: Principles of Building AI Agents (3rd ed.)
license: Free with email signup, all rights reserved
why: A short practical overview of agents, tools, memory, workflows and evals from a framework vendor.
notes: Free with an email signup. Written by Mastra, so examples lean on its framework.

title: Algorithms for Decision Making
authors: Mykel J. Kochenderfer, Tim A. Wheeler, Kyle H. Wray
license: Free PDF from the authors (MIT Press)
why: Rigorous treatment of planning under uncertainty, MDPs, POMDPs and multi-agent decisions behind agent design.

title: The RLHF Book
license: Free online (web and PDF), print edition from Manning
why: The most complete account of RLHF, preference tuning, reward models and post-training for LLMs.

title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: Advanced Topics
why: A wide survey of generative models, inference, RL and decision making at research level.

title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
authors: Marc Peter Deisenroth, A. Aldo Faisal, Cheng Soon Ong
license: Free PDF from the authors (Cambridge University Press)
why: Linear algebra, calculus, probability and optimization taught only as far as machine learning needs them.

title: Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th edition
why: Proof-based linear algebra built around operators, a strong base for understanding matrices in ML.

title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
why: Modern, thorough coverage of probability, statistics and ML models in one coherent notation.

title: The Matrix Calculus You Need For Deep Learning
why: Short, worked derivation of the gradients behind backpropagation, written for programmers.
notes: A long article rather than a full book.

title: Crafting Interpreters
why: Builds two complete interpreters from scratch and teaches how programming languages actually run.
notes: Free web edition. Print and ebook are paid.

title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs, 2nd ed.
authors: Harold Abelson, Gerald Jay Sussman, Julie Sussman
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (MIT Press open access, license not shown on this page)
why: The classic on abstraction, recursion and interpreters that shapes how many engineers think about programs.

title: Algorithms
why: A rigorous, readable algorithms text covering recursion, dynamic programming, graphs and NP-hardness.

title: How to Scale Your Model
authors: Jacob Austin, Sholto Douglas, Roy Frostig, and others (Google DeepMind)
why: Teaches rooflines, sharding, parallelism and LLM inference arithmetic so you can reason about performance from first principles.
notes: Written for TPUs and JAX, but the math transfers to GPUs.

title: The Ultra-Scale Playbook: Training LLMs on GPU Clusters
why: Explains data, tensor, pipeline and context parallelism with measured results from large GPU runs.

title: The Smol Training Playbook
authors: Hugging Face (Loubna Ben Allal and others)
license: Free online (license not stated on the Space)
why: A candid account of the data, ablation and infrastructure decisions in training a small LLM end to end.

title: Machine Learning Systems: The AI Engineering Textbook
why: A full textbook on building, optimizing and deploying ML systems from data pipelines to hardware.

title: Machine Learning Engineering Open Book
why: Practical notes on GPUs, networking, storage, SLURM, debugging and scaling LLM training from a veteran practitioner.

title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
authors: Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau
why: The most readable OS textbook, organized around virtualization, concurrency and persistence.
notes: Every chapter is a free PDF.

title: Basics of 3D Printing with Josef Prusa
license: Free e-book with email signup, copyright Prusa Research
why: A clear guide to FFF printing, slicer settings, materials and troubleshooting from the maker of the printers.
notes: Free with an email signup, or $5 without one.

title: Additive Manufacturing Essentials
authors: John E. Barnes, Timothy W. Simpson (OpenStax)
why: Open textbook covering AM processes, materials, design for AM and file preparation across technologies, not only FDM.

title: OpenSCAD User Manual
why: The reference for code-based CAD, the quickest way to make parametric parts for 3D printing.
notes: A manual for code-based CAD, free on Wikibooks.
